papers.citation: Ho, Chiu Man; Minic, Djordje; Ng, Y. Jack, 'Cold Dark Matter with MOND Scaling', Phys.Lett.B 693 567 (2010), doi:10.1016/j.physletb.2010.09.008 (v1 title: 'MONDian Dark Matter')
papers.read_how: full text, arXiv HTML (v3, 13 Sep 2010) via tools/lit.py; v1 PDF (19 May 2010) read with pypdf to date the key sentences, all of which are in v1

statements.quote: We propose a duality between cold dark matter and modified Newtonian dynamics (MOND).
statements.reading: The 'duality' is between two descriptions of one force law (dark matter as a source, or modified gravity). It is not a dual matter sector and has no conjugate coordinate. Nothing here corresponds to #11's polarization (P2′, P5).

statements.quote: On one hand, we can interpret Eq. (11) to mean that there is no dark matter, but that the law of gravity is modified.
statements.reading: The other reading of Eq. (11) is dark matter with the profile M′ = (1/π)(a0/a)²M, introduced with 'we propose' (Eq. 10), where a0 = √(Λ/3). The tie between dark and baryonic mass is a proposed profile, not a result of dark-matter dynamics.

statements.quote: The above computation suggests that one can in principle have Einstein's gravity together with a MONDian dark matter source.
statements.reading: GR is kept. The paper finds the Friedmann equations unchanged ('exactly the same as the usual ones', same section; also code-checked FOUND), and the dark matter gravitates as an ordinary source. In that respect it is like #11 §8's χ ('propagates on g'). The difference is that its distribution is tied to the baryons and to Λ.

statements.quote: The couplings of MONDian dark matter to the Standard Model particles could be nonstandard, and perhaps even of a spin-orbit type, as implied by remarkable particle physics realizations of the Unruh effect
statements.reading: A speculation ('could be'), with no Lagrangian and no strength given. It is the only mention in the 2010 paper of a coupling to Standard Model particles beyond gravity; under #11 P4, taken strictly, there is none. It is present in v1.

statements.quote: In our proposal, the total mass of MONDian dark matter is related to the cosmological constant as well as the total mass of ordinary matter. This seems to suggest that the microscopic MONDian dark matter degrees of freedom would know about the cosmological constant.
statements.reading: The tie is stated as a property of the profile and of the quanta (they 'would know about the cosmological constant'; the next sentence calls this a 'non-locality'). It is not stated as a force between dark matter and baryons.

statements.quote: Apparently, at the galactic scale, the MONDian dark matter quanta should be massless to realize the MOND-like behavior. However, at the cluster and cosmological scales, they should become massive and hence CDM-like.
statements.reading: A scale-dependent mass for the quanta, offered heuristically from a holographic (dS/CFT) picture. There is no self-interaction, no dependence on relative velocity and no localization in momentum (contrast the gated self-force of #11 §8).

statements.quote: The usual way of determining the effective mass of CDM particles is to first assume some couplings to the Standard Model particles and impose some “parity-like” quantum numbers that insure stable dark matter.
statements.reading: The paragraph ends 'This logic should be repeatable in our case.' (also code-checked: FOUND, full text). The authors expect the usual analysis of couplings, cross sections and relic abundance to apply. No permanent null is contemplated (contrast #11 §13 row 7).

papers.summary: The founding MDM paper. It reads Milgrom's law as dark matter, using Verlinde's entropic force taken to de Sitter space (the net Unruh temperature (√(a²+a0²) − a0)/2π, a formula it credits to Milgrom 1999), and proposes the profile M′ = (1/π)(a0/a)²M, which ties the dark mass to the baryonic mass and to Λ. GR and the Friedmann equations are unchanged. Its 'duality' is CDM–MOND, two readings of one force law. Couplings to Standard Model particles are only speculated (nonstandard, perhaps spin-orbit). There is no dual sector, momentum space, monopole or polarization.

papers.citation: Ho, Chiu Man; Minic, Djordje; Ng, Y. Jack, 'Quantum Gravity and Dark Matter', Gen.Rel.Grav. 43 2567 (2011); Int.J.Mod.Phys.D 20 2887 (2011) (Gravity Research Foundation essay, fifth prize 2011)
papers.read_how: full text, arXiv HTML (v1) via tools/lit.py

statements.quote: while the second form means that there is dark matter (which, by construction, is consistent with MOND) but that the law of gravity is not modified.
statements.reading: The CDM–MOND duality again. In the dark-matter reading gravity is unmodified, and the profile relates M′, Λ and M (M′ ∼ (√Λ/G)^{1/2} M^{1/2} r for a ≪ a0).

statements.quote: in terms of an ensemble sum over the entangled left and right Rindler vacuum
statements.reading: 'Entangled' here means the left and right Rindler vacua (and de Sitter static patches) in a thermo-field expansion of the vacuum. It does not mean dark and visible matter. From this the paper argues that inertia becomes acceleration- and Λ-dependent ('This general argument suggests that Milgrom’s scaling is just a new physical phenomenon in which the inertial properties are acceleration- and' [Λ-dependent], also code-checked FOUND).

statements.quote: In addition we have argued that the inertia of matter is quantum gravitational and is deeply connected to dark energy.
statements.reading: The dark–baryon tie is placed in inertia and in Λ, a property of the vacuum, not in an interaction between the sectors.

statements.quote: That same relation seems to suggest that the microscopic MONDian dark matter degrees of freedom may have knowledge of the non-local cosmological constant; what are some of the phenomenological implications (for example, in dark matter searches)?
statements.reading: The implications for dark-matter searches are posed as an open question. No direct-detection prediction is made.

papers.summary: A short essay restating MDM: the CDM–MOND duality, a profile relating dark matter, Λ and ordinary matter, and an argument that inertia is acceleration- and Λ-dependent, drawn from an expansion of the de Sitter vacuum in entangled static patches. It names no coupling, no detection signature and no dual sector.

papers.citation: Ho, Chiu Man; Minic, Djordje; Ng, Y. Jack, 'Dark Matter, Infinite Statistics and Quantum Gravity', Phys.Rev.D 85 104033 (2012)
papers.read_how: full text, arXiv HTML (v3, 28 Apr 2012) via tools/lit.py; v1 and v2 not read

statements.quote: We then argue that these unconventional quanta of MONDian dark matter must obey infinite statistics, and the theory must be fundamentally non-local.
statements.reading: A property of the quanta: infinite (quantum Boltzmann) statistics with the Cuntz algebra a_i a_j† = δ_ij. The argument needs it so that equipartition holds at the very low effective temperature (the paper: k_B T_eff ∼ 10⁻²⁴ eV for a = 10 m/s²; by code 3.5×10⁻²⁴ eV and 4.1×10⁻²⁰ K). The 2017 review offers this property as the microscopic basis of the dark–baryon correlation.

statements.quote: Since we keep the equivalence principle intact in our arguments and do not introduce any new local gravitational degrees of freedom, we do not modify general relativity. Thus these nonstandard degrees of freedom in the effective gravitational Born-Infeld theory will essentially manifest as new particle degrees of freedom.
statements.reading: GR is unmodified; the MOND-like behaviour is carried by new matter degrees of freedom.

statements.quote: Such phenomenological studies will crucially rely on a non-local propagator of the infinite statistics quanta, as well as their interactions with the Standard Model particles.
statements.reading: Interactions with Standard Model particles are needed for phenomenology but are not specified.

statements.quote: is the relevant standard model operator that describes the necessary coupling to the dark matter sector
statements.where: section 5, Conclusion, the matrix model of Eq. (31)
statements.reading: In a speculative top-down sketch, L = Tr(½(∂𝕄)² + m²𝕄² + g V(𝕄) O_SM), the 'Yukawa' coupling g to a Standard Model operator O_SM is called 'necessary' and treated as a phenomenological parameter. This is the only written non-gravitational coupling in the MDM papers. It belongs to a toy model, is neither fitted nor derived, and is not connected to the acceleration-scale correlation. Under #11 P4 strict no such coupling exists.

statements.quote: We naturally expect that such non-canonical dark matter quanta should have dramatic signatures in high energy particle experiments.
statements.reading: Expects signals at high-energy experiments. No null is predicted (contrast #11 §13 row 7, 'Permanent null').

statements.quote: Naturally we are led to conjecture that the application of the same experimental techniques may be relevant in the observational search of MONDian dark matter with infinite statistics.
statements.reading: A conjecture that search techniques for primordial black holes may apply. No specific signal is given.

statements.quote: At the moment, it seems prohibitive to check this prediction in astronomical observations.
statements.reading: In 2012 the galactic profile is judged not yet checkable. The 2013 paper (1308.3252) then fits rotation curves.

statements.quote: we first point out a surprising connection between the MONDian dark matter and an effective gravitational Born-Infeld theory
statements.reading: 'Born-Infeld' is Born and Infeld's nonlinear electrodynamics (the paper's Eq. 6, cited through Gibbons' review [26]), used as a gravitational dielectric analogy for the force law. It is not Born reciprocity (#11 §3).

papers.summary: Argues that MDM quanta obey infinite statistics and are therefore non-local, notes that the MDM force law matches a gravitational Born–Infeld Hamiltonian, and sketches a matrix model with a phenomenological coupling to a Standard Model operator. GR is unmodified. It expects dramatic signatures in high-energy experiments. There is no dual sector.

papers.citation: Edmonds, Doug; Farrah, Duncan; Ho, Chiu Man; Minic, Djordje; Ng, Y. Jack; Takeuchi, Tatsu, 'Testing MONDian Dark Matter with Galactic Rotation Curves', Astrophys.J. 793 41 (2014), doi:10.1088/0004-637X/793/1/41
papers.read_how: full text, arXiv HTML (v2, 15 Jul 2014) via tools/lit.py, including Table 1; v1 not read

statements.quote: we provide the first observational test of MDM by fitting rotation curves to a sample of 30 local spiral galaxies
statements.reading: Data: the 30 Ursa Major spirals of Sanders & Verheijen (1998), z ≈ 0.003 (21 cm rotation curves, K′-band photometry). Fits use a_c = 1.2×10⁻⁸ from Begeman et al. (printed 'cm s-1'), and the mass-to-light ratio M/L is the only free parameter for MDM and MOND ('which is our only fitting parameter for MDM and MOND, is assumed constant for a given galaxy but allowed to vary between galaxies', §III.2, code-checked FOUND). Errors come from fits to one hundred randomized data sets; NFW has three free parameters.

statements.quote: We find that all three models fit the data well. The rotation curves predicted by MDM and MOND are virtually indistinguishable over the range of observed radii
statements.reading: Result: CDM (NFW), MOND and MDM all fit, and MDM and MOND agree over ∼1 to 30 kpc. In nearly a third of the galaxies the NFW fits give too large a virial mass (NGC 4389: v200 ≈ 1000 km/s, ≈ 5×10¹⁴ M⊙).

statements.quote: instead of continuing to rise sharply, the MDM mass density turns over and drops as we approach the center of the galaxy
statements.reading: The discriminating prediction against MOND read as dark matter: a central turnover. For a Milky Way-sized disk the paper puts it at r < 1 kpc (by code r_c = √(GM/a_c) = 10.8 kpc for M = 10¹¹ M⊙, so 0.1 r_c = 1.08 kpc).

statements.quote: Whether such a dark matter profile can be realized dynamically will depend on the detailed nature of the MDM quanta and their interactions with ordinary matter.
statements.reading: Central to Q4: the profile is a phenomenological input. How it arises dynamically, including any interaction with ordinary matter, is left to the unknown nature of the quanta.

statements.quote: Our approach differs from these papers in the crucial fact that it assumes an actual source of dark matter, which, however, is not of a traditional particle type (i.e. it is not described by a local effective quantum field theory).
statements.reading: MDM is a real dark-matter source but not a local particle. This is the property the authors rely on; no coupling is specified.

statements.quote: In the CDM paradigm, accelerations are determined by General Relativity and the addition of massive particles that interact only gravitationally, dark matter.
statements.reading: Their CDM is gravity-only. MDM is set apart from it by Λ ('In MDM, the critical acceleration is introduced through the cosmological constant', same paragraph, code-checked FOUND) and by the nature of the quanta, not by a stated non-gravitational interaction.

statements.quote: in the hopes that the model's predictions can be checked against data from experiments such as Fermi-LAT
statements.reading: Indirect detection: a hope that gamma-ray maps could test the predicted profile; footnote 4 adds that such signals could be astrophysical (pulsars). The paper does not say what would produce the gamma rays (my observation).

statements.quote: Besides obeying different statistics, MDM has some unusual inertial properties (see Equation (A9)). This provides a natural explanation for the measured underdensity of dark matter in the solar system
statements.reading: The paper continues that the External Field Effect 'is built into the inertial properties of MDM, so we do not expect to see dark matter effects in the Solar system' (code-checked FOUND), and notes Bovy & Tremaine's contrary, standard density. My inference: a lower local density would lower direct-detection rates; the paper does not draw this.

papers.summary: The first data test of MDM. It fits 30 Ursa Major rotation curves with M/L as the one free parameter: MDM, MOND and NFW all fit, MDM matches MOND over 1–30 kpc, and MDM predicts a central density turnover. The profile is reverse-engineered, and its dynamical realization, including any interaction with ordinary matter, is left open. The quanta are non-local, possibly with infinite statistics.

papers.citation: Edmonds, Doug; Farrah, Duncan; Ho, Chi man; Minic, Djordje; Ng, Y. Jack; Takeuchi, Tatsu, 'Testing Modified Dark Matter with Galaxy Clusters: Does Dark Matter know about the Cosmological Constant?', Int.J.Mod.Phys.A 32 1750108 (2017), doi:10.1142/S0217751X17501081

statements.quote: so the dark matter must track the baryonic matter
statements.reading: M′ ∝ M, so the dark matter tracks the baryons by construction of the profile. The paper adds that M′ depends on a_c, read as 'the dark matter being knowledgable about the Hubble parameter'.

statements.quote: Despite its appearance, Eq. (18) does not modify General Relativity (GR) since the derivation of the right-hand-side is based on GR.
statements.reading: Einstein's equations are unchanged. The MDM relation is a_N[1 + f_MDM(a/a0)] = √(a² + a0²) − a0, with a0 = c²√(Λ/3) = cH0 = 2πa_c (Eq. 20). By code, cH0 = 6.58×10⁻¹⁰ m/s² for H0 = 67.74 km/s/Mpc (paper: (6.581 ± 0.045)×10⁻⁸ cm/s²).

statements.quote: is conveyed to the dark-matter via the temperature of the de Sitter horizon
statements.reading: The channel by which the dark matter 'knows' Λ is the de Sitter horizon temperature: a thermodynamic statement, not a force between dark matter and baryons.

statements.quote: This choice is, of course, arbitrary and a case of reverse engineering.
statements.reading: The authors' own word for the 2010–2014 profile f_MDM = (1/π)(a0/a)². Section 2 then motivates (1/2)(a0/a)² by a Jacobson-type thermodynamic argument. They add 'Despite lacking a dynamical theory, which precludes performing numerical simulations,' (code-checked FOUND).

statements.quote: Thus the energy momentum tensor of the extra sources (which we will identify with missing mass) has to be related to the energy momentum tensor of ordinary visible matter
statements.reading: The relation is between stress tensors, T′_αβ = (a0²/2a²)T_αβ (Eq. 36) and M′ = (a0²/2a²)M (Eq. 37): a proportionality fixed by temperatures, with no interaction term. My reading of Eq. 37: a0² = c⁴Λ/3, so M′ ∝ Λ at fixed a.

statements.quote: Our dark matter mass profile thus “knows” about the visible matter as well as the cosmological background
statements.reading: The paper's own phrasing of the tie: the profile 'knows' about visible matter, about the background and about inertia. The section closes 'From our perspective, flat galactic rotation curves are a quantum gravity effect at large scales.' (code-checked FOUND).

statements.quote: We have shown that MDM performs as well as CDM, and considerably better than MOND (which only works well at the galactic scale), for all clusters in our sample.
statements.reading: Data: 13 low-redshift relaxed clusters of Vikhlinin et al. 2006 (Chandra, with ROSAT-PSPC where deep enough; 0.7–9 keV; hydrostatic masses). The authors assign a 1σ error of 10%. The generalized profile f = α/[1 + r/r_MDM](a0/a)² fits with α ∼ 100 and r_MDM ∼ 10 kpc, and galaxies are refit with α = 0.5 and r_MDM = 20 kpc. MOND fails in both magnitude and shape.

statements.quote: needs to change by two orders of magnitude. This is not completely unrealistic, given our heuristic thermodynamic reasoning, but we have to admit of being ignorant of the underlying reason for this.
statements.reading: Against-evidence stated by the authors: α must change by two orders of magnitude (∼1 to ∼100; log10 = 2.0 by code) between galaxies and clusters, for no known reason.

statements.quote: A more concrete theory for MDM quanta will allow us to test this idea at colliders, dark matter direct detection experiments and indirect detection experiments.
statements.reading: Detection is deferred to a future concrete theory. No null is predicted (contrast #11 §13 row 7).

statements.quote: For example, such unusual non-local quanta could be found in recent reformulations of quantum gravity and string theory
statements.where: section 4, Discussion (followed by citations of Freidel, Leigh & Minic 2013, 2014, 2015)
statements.reading: The earliest MDM pointer to the Freidel–Leigh–Minic reformulations, offered as a possible home for the quanta. It says nothing about the quanta being the dual of visible matter. The 2010–2013 MDM texts contain no mention of Freidel, metastrings or metaparticles (my count over their full texts: 0).

statements.quote: we plan to study the constraints from gravitational lensing and colliding clusters such as the Bullet Cluster
statements.reading: Colliding-cluster and lensing tests are planned, not done.

papers.summary: Renames MONDian dark matter as Modified Dark Matter. It derives the profile M′ = (a0²/2a²)M from a Jacobson-type argument in which the de Sitter temperature shifts the energy at fixed entropy, with GR unmodified and Λ entering through the horizon temperature. A generalized profile is fitted to 13 Chandra clusters (α ∼ 100, r_MDM ∼ 10 kpc), and the authors concede that α changes by two orders of magnitude from galaxies for no known reason. Its discussion gives the earliest MDM pointer to Freidel–Leigh–Minic.

papers.citation: Ng, Y. Jack; Edmonds, Doug; Farrah, Duncan; Minic, Djordje; Takeuchi, Tatsu; Ho, Chiu Man, 'Modified Dark Matter', conference paper, 14th Marcel Grossmann Meeting proceedings (2017), doi:10.1142/9789813226609_0524
papers.read_how: full text, arXiv HTML via tools/lit.py

statements.quote: Modified dark matter (MDM, formerly known as MoNDian dark matter) is a phenomenological model of dark matter, inspired by quantum gravity.
statements.reading: The authors' self-description: phenomenological.

statements.quote: Unlike cold dark matter models, the MDM mass profile depends on the baryonic mass.
statements.reading: The defining contrast with CDM is a baryon-dependent profile, not a stated interaction.

statements.quote: how strongly coupled is MDM to baryonic matter and how does MDM self-interact?
statements.where: section 1, list of future work, item 2
statements.reading: In 2016 the strength of MDM's coupling to baryons and its self-interaction are open questions, listed with 'unusual particle phenomenology?' and the Bullet Cluster. MDM states no coupling beyond gravity, and does not rule one out.

statements.quote: We show that dynamical and observed masses agree in a sample of 93 galactic clusters.
statements.reading: Data: 93 X-ray clusters (White, Jones & Forman 1997, as analysed by Sanders 1999). Sanders found ⟨M_N/M_obs⟩ ≈ 4.4 and ⟨M_MOND/M_obs⟩ ≈ 2.1. With the general profile M′ = [ξ(a0/a) + (1/π)(a0/a)²]M and a universal ξ ≈ 0.5, the paper gets ⟨M_MDM/M_obs⟩ ≈ 1.0, and refitting the galaxies with ξ = 0.5 gives nearly identical fits with M/L lower by about 35%. Strong lensing 'appears' sufficient because a0 = cH0 = 2πa_c ≈ 6a_c (2π = 6.28 by code).

statements.quote: Note added: This discussion has since been superseded by more recent work by the authors.
statements.reading: The ξ-profile is superseded by the α/(1 + r/r_MDM) form of 1601.00662.

papers.summary: A conference review of MDM: the construction, the 30-galaxy fits (one free parameter, against three for NFW), and a 93-cluster comparison in which a linear term ξ ≈ 0.5 removes the virial discrepancy (⟨M_MDM/M_obs⟩ ≈ 1.0). It lists MDM's coupling to baryons and its self-interaction as open questions.

papers.citation: Edmonds, Douglas; Farrah, Duncan; Minic, Djordje; Ng, Y. Jack; Takeuchi, Tatsu, 'Modified Dark Matter: Relating Dark Energy, Dark Matter and Baryonic Matter', Int.J.Mod.Phys.D 27 1830001 (2017), doi:10.1142/S021827181830001X

statements.quote: The defining feature of the MDM proposal is that the modified dark matter profile should be sensitive to the fundamental acceleration
statements.reading: The sentence continues: 'or alternatively, to the cosmological constant, at all scales (galactic, cluster and cosmological) and that on galactic scales the modified dark matter mass profile should be correlated to the baryonic mass profile' (second part code-checked FOUND). The correlation is a property required of the profile.

statements.quote: However, we also aim to have enough flexibility not to correlate the dark matter mass profile to the baryonic mass profile on cluster and cosmological scales.
statements.reading: The correlation is meant to switch off on cluster and cosmological scales. That is the scale limit in which it vanishes (Q4).

statements.quote: On the other hand, this correlation could be pointing to a yet unknown property of DM which connects its distribution to that of baryonic matter.
statements.reading: The data behind 'correlation': the RAR with ā0 = (1.20 ± 0.02)×10⁻¹⁰ m/s² and the BTFR with A = (47 ± 6) M⊙ s⁴/km⁴, against 63 from MOND's normalization. By code, 1/(ā0G) = 62.8 M⊙ s⁴/km⁴, and A = 47 ± 6 implies a0 = 1.60 (1.42–1.84)×10⁻¹⁰ m/s².

statements.quote: since some dispersion might be expected between the collision-less CDM particles, and the free baryons that act as fuel for the star formation. Nevertheless, it may be possible to reconcile this result with CDM models
statements.reading: The authors allow that the correlation might be reproduced in gravity-only CDM with dissipative baryons (refs. 87, 58).

statements.quote: Here we emphasize one very important point. Given the fact that we have not changed Einstein's equations, we cannot change the Newton law of motion.
statements.reading: Einstein's equations and Newton's law of motion are unchanged.

statements.quote: To summarize: dark matter exists in our scheme, but its mass profile is tied to the baryonic mass profile (at least on galactic scales) via the observed acceleration and the fundamental acceleration parameter, set by the cosmological constant.
statements.reading: The tie runs through a_obs and a0 within unchanged dynamics (Eq. 36: a_obs = G(M + M′)/r², with M′/M = ½a0²/[(a_obs + a0)² − a0²]).

statements.quote: Such dark matter is most probably of a non-local, non-particle kind, because of the fact that its mass profile is tied to the baryonic mass profiles as well as to the inertial properties, encoded in the observed acceleration.
statements.reading: The inference runs from the profile to the quanta: because the profile is tied to the baryons and to inertia, the quanta must be non-local.

statements.quote: But what is the microscopic basis for this correlation? We will now argue that it may have something to do with the quanta of MDM being non-local (and non-particle-like)
statements.reading: The review's own answer to Q4: the microscopic basis of the correlation is sought in the quanta's non-locality and infinite statistics, not in an interaction.

statements.quote: It is very hard to see why the mass profiles coming from particle-like quanta of some local effective field theory would be sensitive to a fundamental acceleration parameter, set by the cosmological scale, even if one assumes some unusual dissipative baryonic dynamics.
statements.reading: Their reason for excluding local particles. My observation: this sits uneasily with section 1, where dissipative baryonic dynamics 'may' reconcile the data with CDM.

statements.quote: At the moment the MDM proposal is not rooted in any fundamental physics, and there is no specific candidate for the MDM quantum.
statements.reading: In September 2017 there is no candidate quantum.

statements.quote: We expect that such non-local excitations (as part of a covariant non-commutative formulation, as implied by the metastring [131, 132]) can serve as unusual dark matter quanta.
statements.reading: A proposal ('we expect') that non-local excitations of the metastring's non-commutative formulation serve as MDM quanta.

statements.quote: Roughly, the zero mode sector looks like two entangled particles, and it could be viewed as a model for modified dark matter quanta discussed in this review, implying, perhaps naturally, the observed relation between dark matter and baryonic mass profiles at certain scales.
statements.where: section 5 (footnote 13: 'metaparticles', theory being developed by Freidel, Kowalski-Glikman, Leigh and Minic)
statements.reading: The metastring zero-mode sector as a model of MDM quanta. 'Entangled' means the two particles of that sector, and their entanglement is offered ('perhaps') as the origin of the dark–baryon profile relation. This is not yet the identification of dark matter as the dual of visible matter.

statements.quote: How strongly coupled is MDM to baryonic matter? How does MDM self-interact?
statements.reading: In 2017 the coupling strength and the self-interaction are still open. Contrast #11 §8, where a velocity-gated self-interaction defines the χ form.

statements.quote: which may explain why, so far, dark matter detection experiments have failed to detect dark matter particles
statements.reading: A hedged ('may') explanation of the null results by non-locality.

statements.quote: A more concrete theory for MDM quanta will allow us to test the whole scheme of MDM at colliders, dark matter direct detection experiments and indirect detection experiments.
statements.reading: Tests at colliders and in direct and indirect detection are deferred to a concrete theory. No permanent null is stated (contrast #11 §13 row 7).

statements.quote: it is possible that there are (dark) stars made of such quanta
statements.reading: A speculation, conditional on infinite statistics. No condensate, wave form or momentum localization is proposed.

statements.quote: Note that we will be treating the dark energy as the cosmological constant or vacuum energy
statements.reading: In MDM dark energy is Λ (w = −1) throughout. Contrast #11 §10 (τ, strictly w ≥ −1, thawing).

statements.quote: Our central observation is that Milgrom's scaling implies a non-local mixing of physics in the dark matter and dark energy sector.
statements.reading: The dark matter–dark energy link is a0 ↔ Λ. Section 4 speculates: 'Conceivably it is the extended nature of the MDM quanta that connects them to the cosmological constant/dark energy and the Hubble parameter' (code-checked FOUND).

statements.quote: for such extended excitations the change in momentum is proportional to the change in distance
statements.reading: A heuristic: δp ∼ αδx together with the ordinary Heisenberg relation δpδx ∼ ħ gives an acceleration ∝ 1/distance, 'exactly what the Milgrom scaling demands'. Momentum here is ordinary momentum at ħ, and there is no conjugate polarization (contrast #11 P2′).

statements.quote: The black squares are 386 data points from a sample of 30 galaxies presented in this paper.
statements.reading: Data: 386 points from the 30 galaxies, fitted with a_obs = a_bar/[1 − exp(−√(a_bar/zā0))]. For the 13 clusters, values of α between ∼50 and 100 fit, values ≲50 do not, and α = 50 is used in the figures. The abstract claims 'the same critical acceleration appears both in the galactic and cluster data fits based on MDM' (code-checked FOUND, abstract), with α changing from ∼1 to 50–100 (§3.2 calls this an effective 'renormalizaton' of a0).

papers.summary: The MDM review. Its defining feature is a dark-matter profile that is Λ-sensitive at all scales and correlated with the baryonic profile on galactic scales only, inside unmodified GR. The correlation's 'microscopic basis' is sought in non-local, infinite-statistics quanta, and the metastring zero-mode sector ('two entangled particles') is proposed as a model for them. Coupling strength to baryons and self-interaction are open. Detection tests await a concrete theory, and non-locality 'may explain' the null results.

papers.citation: Edmonds, Douglas; Farrah, Duncan; Minic, Djordje; Ng, Y. Jack; Takeuchi, Tatsu, 'Modified Dark Matter in Galaxies and Galaxy Clusters', Bulg.J.Phys. 45 138 (2018) (BASIC 2017 proceedings)
papers.read_how: full text, arXiv HTML via tools/lit.py, all sections and references

statements.quote: The aforementioned MDAR indicates a coupling between DM and BM governed by a universal acceleration scale
statements.reading: Here the authors call the mass-discrepancy acceleration relation a 'coupling' between dark and baryonic matter, without saying of what kind. Nothing in the paper makes it a force or an interaction term.

statements.quote: One of the attributes of the MDM model is that it must decouple from baryons at the cosmological scale. Exactly how this de-coupling occurs is currently under investigation.
statements.reading: The 'coupling' must vanish at cosmological scales, and how is unknown. The paper adds 'Since baryons should not be sensitive to' Λ, the a0 in the data is attributed to the dark matter (code-checked FOUND).

statements.quote: We do not, however, expect the correlation between DM and BM to be as tight in galaxy clusters as it is in galaxies.
statements.reading: The cluster correlation is looser: 13 clusters, and 12 with M2500 for the M_dyn–M_bar plot ('the correlation is not very tight').

statements.quote: the correlations could be pointing to yet unknown properties of DM which connects its distribution to that of BM at galactic scales, yet allows for de-coupling at cosmological scales.
statements.reading: Again a property of dark matter, not a specified interaction.

answers.question: Q1
answers.answer: No MDM paper (2010–2024) states that dark matter is the dual or conjugate counterpart of visible matter. MDM's 'duality' is the CDM–MOND duality, one force law read either as modified gravity or as dark matter with a proposed profile, and in 2017 the review says 'there is no specific candidate for the MDM quantum'. The steps toward the dual sector, each a pointer, proposal or speculation: (1) 4 Jan 2016 (1601.00662 §4), a pointer: such non-local quanta 'could be found' in the Freidel–Leigh–Minic reformulations. (2) 13 Sep 2017 (1709.04388 §5), a proposal: metastring excitations 'can serve as unusual dark matter quanta', and the zero-mode sector, 'two entangled particles', 'could be viewed as a model for modified dark matter quanta'. (3) 30 Dec 2017 (1801.00160 §5), a speculation: MDM quanta 'might be modeled as metaparticles ... two entangled particles in momentum space'; the record does not mention this paper. (4) 18 May 2020 (2005.08927), inside 'Let us speculate', metaparticles as 'A possible candidate'. The identification of MDM's quanta with the dual cousins of Standard Model fields is made outside the MDM papers, in Minic 2020 (2003.00318, 29 Feb 2020): 'the natural model for MDM quanta could be provided by the metaparticle realizations of the Standard Model particles', with the baryons' 'natural cousins (the Ã backgrounds ...)' in the dark sector; that is a proposal. Edmonds, Minic and Takeuchi repeat it in 2021 (2109.12763: 'Thus the entire SM would have a dual SM (which we propose, describes the dark matter sector)'). The later observational papers of the MDM line (2009.12915, Sep 2020; 2405.08744, May 2024) do not mention the dual sector, metaparticles or Born geometry (word counts 0). Relative to #11 App. A item 4, the MDM line is a precursor of the school's identification, not a statement of C1.

answers.question: Q2
answers.answer: Not addressed in the MDM papers. They define no dual coordinate x̃ and give no commutators [x, x̃], [x, p] or [x̃, p̃]. 'Dual' means the CDM–MOND duality (1005.3537, 1105.2916, 1308.3252), a holographic dual (dS/CFT, 1005.3537), or T-duality in passing (1709.04388 §5). The 'Born-Infeld theory' of 1201.2365 is Born and Infeld's nonlinear electrodynamics, used as a gravitational dielectric analogy, not Born reciprocity. Momentum appears twice. 1801.00160 speaks of 'two entangled particles in momentum space' without defining it. 1709.04388 §5 has a heuristic δp ∼ αδx with the ordinary Heisenberg relation δpδx ∼ ħ, so momentum there is ordinary momentum at ħ. MDM's scales are ħ (Unruh temperature), G and a0 = c²√(Λ/3) = cH0; there is no string scale λ. λ (UV) and L (IR) enter only in the string-side papers, in Berglund–Hübsch–Minić 2021's mixing term ∝ λ⁸/L¹⁰. Nothing in MDM corresponds to the program's polarization of one phase space with ω rigid (#11 P2′, P5).

answers.question: Q3
answers.answer: MDM has no dual copy of the Standard Model, no dual photon and no dual charges. What the papers say about the quanta: massless at galactic scales and massive (CDM-like) at cluster scales, and 'vector and scalar degrees of freedom may be preferred' (1005.3537, speculative); infinite statistics (Cuntz algebra), 'fundamentally non-local', with a toy 'neutral scalar field obeying infinite statistics' (1201.2365); 'not of a traditional particle type (i.e. it is not described by a local effective quantum field theory)' (1308.3252); 'most probably of a non-local, non-particle kind' (1709.04388). The 2012 top-down sketch is an infinite matrix 𝕄 with a phenomenological 'Yukawa' coupling g to a Standard Model operator. In 2024 (2405.08744) the dark matter is an ultralight boson of ∼10⁻²² eV, 'perhaps axion-like'. A partner for every Standard Model field appears only in the string-side papers: Minic 2020 (metaparticle realizations of SM particles, A and Ã, a photon and its dual), and Edmonds–Minic–Takeuchi 2021 ('the entire SM would have a dual SM'). MDM has no analog of #11 P4's p-polarized representations or of §11.4's magnetic mirror.

answers.question: Q4
answers.answer: In MDM's own papers the tie between dark matter and baryons is not a written interaction. It has three layers. (1) An observed regularity: the radial acceleration (mass-discrepancy) relation and the baryonic Tully–Fisher and Faber–Jackson relations, with an acceleration of order 10⁻¹⁰ m/s² ≈ cH0/2π. The authors call it 'an observational fact, which is independent of any theoretical assumptions' and say 'Occam's razor would favor' its emergence within gravity-only ΛCDM (2005.08927); 2009.12915 calls that 'The simplest' explanation; the 2017 review allows that 'it may be possible to reconcile this result with CDM models'. (2) A phenomenological mass profile, M′ = f(a/a0)·M: (1/π)(a0/a)² in 2010–2014, (1/2)(a0/a)² from a Jacobson-type de Sitter argument in 2016–2017, times α/(1 + r/r_MDM) with α ≈ 1 (0.5) in galaxies and 50–100 in clusters. Einstein's equations are unchanged ('Despite its appearance, Eq. (18) does not modify General Relativity'; 'we have not changed Einstein's equations'). Λ reaches the dark matter 'via the temperature of the de Sitter horizon'. The profile is 'arbitrary and a case of reverse engineering', 'lacking a dynamical theory', and the relation is a proportionality of stress tensors, T′_αβ = (a0²/2a²)T_αβ (1601.00662). (3) A property attributed to the quanta: knowledge of Λ, infinite statistics, non-locality; 'the microscopic basis for this correlation ... may have something to do with the quanta of MDM being non-local' (1709.04388 §4). So, among Q4's options, MDM's tie is a phenomenological profile plus a property of the dark quanta. It is not a stated non-gravitational interaction, and no coupling strength is ever given. Couplings to Standard Model particles appear only as speculation: 'could be nonstandard, and perhaps even of a spin-orbit type' (2010), and a toy matrix model with a 'Yukawa' coupling g to an SM operator, 'the necessary coupling to the dark matter sector' (2012), not linked to the acceleration correlation. The strength stays open: 'how strongly coupled is MDM to baryonic matter and how does MDM self-interact?' (2016, 2017). In 2017 (1801.00160) the authors call the relation 'a coupling between DM and BM governed by a universal acceleration scale' that 'must decouple from baryons at the cosmological scale. Exactly how this de-coupling occurs is currently under investigation'. In 2024 (2405.08744) the link is gravity alone: fuzzy dark matter in equilibrium between quantum and gravitational potentials, 'with the gravitational potential providing a link between the baryonic and dark matter'. What 'correlated' and 'entangled' mean in my papers: the observed relations and the profile; in 2011, the entangled left and right Rindler vacua; in 2017, the 'two entangled particles' of the metastring zero-mode sector, offered ('perhaps') as the origin of the profile relation, and later 'in momentum space'. The explicit non-gravitational terms are in the string-side papers that adopt MDM as their observed side: Minic 2020's Berry-phase-like 'metaparticle entanglement' term α′A_μ dÃ^μ/dt, 'uniquely different from the usual effective field theory interaction terms'; Berglund–Hübsch–Minić 2021's mixing term −(λ⁸/L¹⁰)f[[A, Ã]], 'invisible in effective field theory', which they identify with the Hubble-scale correlation 'studied in the context of modified dark matter'; Edmonds–Minic–Takeuchi 2021, 'correlated to the visible sector via the dark energy sector' (their Ref. 12, the MDM papers); Hübsch–Minić 2024, 'correlated (via the minimal length' λ). Limits: the MDM correlation is meant to switch off on cluster and cosmological scales (1709.04388 §2; 1801.00160), and by my reading of 1601.00662 Eq. (37), M′ ∝ a0² ∝ Λ at fixed a; the BHM term vanishes as λ → 0 or L → ∞. Against the program: #11 P4 strict allows no coupling beyond gravity (ε ≲ 10⁻¹³). My inference is that the school's 'correlated' differs from the program's gravity-only sector through the string-side terms, not through MDM's data, which the MDM authors themselves allow to arise by gravity alone.

answers.question: Q5
answers.answer: Data and fits, numbers as printed. Galaxies (1308.3252): the 30 Ursa Major spirals of Sanders & Verheijen, z ≈ 0.003; a_c = 1.2×10⁻⁸ (printed 'cm s-1'); M/L is the one free parameter for MDM and MOND, against three for NFW; 'all three models fit the data well', and MDM and MOND are 'virtually indistinguishable' over ∼1–30 kpc. The prediction against MOND is a central turnover of the MDM density (r < 1 kpc for a Milky Way-sized galaxy; by code 0.1r_c = 1.08 kpc). Clusters: 93 X-ray clusters (1602.00055) give ⟨M_N/M_obs⟩ ≈ 4.4, ⟨M_MOND/M_obs⟩ ≈ 2.1 and ⟨M_MDM/M_obs⟩ ≈ 1.0 with ξ ≈ 0.5, a result the authors say is superseded. 13 Chandra clusters of Vikhlinin et al. (1601.00662): MDM 'performs as well as CDM, and considerably better than MOND', with α ∼ 100 and r_MDM ∼ 10 kpc (α ∼ 50–100 in 1709.04388), against α ≈ 1 (0.5 with r_MDM = 20 kpc) in galaxies, a change of two orders of magnitude the authors 'admit' they cannot explain. The 2017 review plots 386 points from the 30 galaxies against the RAR, with ā0 = (1.20 ± 0.02)×10⁻¹⁰ m/s² and BTFR A = (47 ± 6) M⊙ s⁴/km⁴ (by code 1/(ā0G) = 62.8, paper 63). Scaling papers: RAR a§ = (1.2 ± 0.02(stat) ± 0.24(syst))×10⁻¹⁰ m/s² from 2693 points in 153 SPARC galaxies; a BFJR with n = 4 over M_bar = 10^{4∼14} M⊙, from 62 HIFLUGCS clusters, 56 ellipticals and 56 globular clusters (2005.08927); BTFR slope (1.6 ± 0.2)a0 and a∅ = (1.5 +1.4/−0.7)a0, with clusters alone preferring n ≈ 3 and n ≈ 4 only jointly, a∅ ≈ 1.4a0 and 1.3a0 (2009.12915); a0 = (1.3 ± 0.3)×10⁻¹⁰ (BTFR) and (1.5 +0.9/−0.6)×10⁻¹⁰ m/s² (E0 galaxies), no redshift dependence to z ≈ 2.5 in 100 RC100 galaxies (2405.08744). By code, cH0/2π = 1.05×10⁻¹⁰ m/s² for H0 = 67.74, so the RAR value is 1.15 times it. Proposed discriminators: the central turnover (2013); strong lensing 'appears' sufficient because a0 = cH0 ≈ 6a_c (2016–17); an acceleration floor ∝ a0 in galaxies but none in clusters (Dec 2017); a0 in colliding clusters would show that a0 is fundamental (2020); a redshift dependence of a0 for the fuzzy-dark-matter account (2024); no dark-matter effects in the solar system, attributed to MDM's built-in External Field Effect (2013); a hope that Fermi-LAT gamma-ray maps test the profile (2013). Direct detection and colliders: 'dramatic signatures in high energy particle experiments' expected (2012); tests 'at colliders, dark matter direct detection experiments and indirect detection experiments' deferred to 'A more concrete theory' (2016, 2017); primordial-black-hole search techniques 'may be relevant' (2012). Null results: non-locality 'may explain why, so far, dark matter detection experiments have failed' (2017 abstract), and Minic 2020 and Edmonds–Minic–Takeuchi 2021 add the conditional 'If the quanta of MDM are metaparticles, this may explain why'. No MDM paper predicts a permanent null (contrast #11 §13 row 7). The program's record has no statement on the acceleration-scale relations: no mention of MOND, Tully–Fisher, Milgrom, Faber–Jackson or the RAR in papers/, notes/ (literature-check.md aside), wiki/, HANDOFF.md or popsci/ (grep).

answers.question: Q6
answers.answer: MDM keeps GR. The Friedmann equations are 'exactly the same as the usual ones' (1005.3537); 'we do not modify general relativity' (1201.2365); Eq. (18) 'does not modify General Relativity' (1601.00662); 'we have not changed Einstein's equations, we cannot change the Newton law of motion' (1709.04388). The dark matter gravitates on the ordinary metric as a source on the right-hand side, with standard Newton's constant G (in the entropic derivation N = Ac³/(Għ)). Λ enters through the de Sitter horizon temperature, not through a dual metric. In 2024 the dark matter and the baryons move in one gravitational potential (2405.08744). MDM itself sets nothing about G. On the string side, Berglund–Hübsch–Minić 2021 write that 'the weakness of gravity is determined by the size of the canonically conjugate dual space, while the smallness of the cosmological constant is given by its curvature'. Compared with #11 §8 (χ propagates on g; equivalence principle), the two agree that dark matter gravitates normally. MDM's distribution is tied to the baryons and Λ by the profile; #11 adds the massive momentum-graviton X, which MDM has no counterpart for.

answers.question: Q7
answers.answer: Self-interaction: never specified; 'how does MDM self-interact?' is an open question in 2016 and 2017, with colliding-cluster (Bullet Cluster, A520) tests planned but not made. No dependence on relative velocity and no overlap of momenta appears anywhere; nothing resembles #11 §8's velocity gate. Momentum: 1801.00160's 'two entangled particles in momentum space' describes the proposed metaparticle model of the quanta, not a localization or clumping of matter in momentum (contrast #11 App. A item 3 and §12's p-localized monopoles); 1709.04388's δp ∼ αδx is a heuristic for extended one-dimensional excitations. Other dynamics: quanta massless at galactic and massive at cluster scales (2010, speculative); infinite statistics and non-locality, possibly with '(dark) stars made of such quanta' (2017, conditional). Wave or fuzzy form: the 2024 essay adopts ordinary fuzzy dark matter, ultralight (10⁻²² eV) particles, a Madelung quantum potential that sets a_FDM ∼ 2×10⁻¹⁰ m/s² (checked 2.2×10⁻¹⁰ with the ½ factor), and 'heavier soliton degrees of freedom' at ∼10⁻¹⁹ eV that structure halos. These solitons are position-space cores; they are not magnetic and not localized in momentum. Hübsch–Minić 2024 later read metaparticles as fuzzy dark matter, citing that essay.

answers.question: Q8

answers.question: Q9
answers.answer: Not addressed in these papers. There is no polarization of phase space, no vacuum selection and no order parameter. The only 'polarization' is Blanchet's gravitational polarization, a MOND alternative cited in 1308.3252 and 1709.04388.

answers.question: Q10
answers.answer: MDM takes dark energy to be the cosmological constant: 'we will be treating the dark energy as the cosmological constant or vacuum energy' (1709.04388; also 1801.00160). Its role is to set the acceleration, a0 = c²√(Λ/3) = cH0 = 2πā0 (1601.00662 Eq. 20), which enters the dark-matter profile: 'Milgrom's scaling implies a non-local mixing of physics in the dark matter and dark energy sector' (1709.04388). Earlier papers hint at a fixed ratio of energy densities that might ease the coincidence problem (2010, 2011). No equation of state other than w = −1 is discussed; there is no phantom or thawing prediction and no collapse. The 2024 essay conjectures that fuzzy dark matter's quantum pressure is related to vacuum energy: a vacuum scale of 10⁻³ eV as the geometric mean of the Hubble and Planck scales (checked 1.0×10⁻³ eV, citing Freidel–Kowalski-Glikman–Leigh–Minic 2023 and Berglund–Hübsch–Minić 2023). That would explain a0 ∼ cH0/2π and predicts an a0 that changes with redshift, not seen to z ∼ 2.5. On the string side, Berglund–Hübsch–Minić 2021 make Λ the curvature of the dual space. Compared with #11 §10 (τ hilltop quintessence, strictly w ≥ −1, thawing; DESI DR2 under pressure): MDM assumes w = −1 and does not address C5, 'Their collapse is our acceleration' (App. A item 9).

answers.question: Q11
answers.answer: MDM begins on 19 May 2010 (1005.3537v1, titled 'MONDian Dark Matter'). It credits its formula to earlier work: Milgrom 1999 for the de Sitter Unruh-temperature difference √(a²+a0²) − a0 ('Milgrom has suggested in [13] ...'), Verlinde 2010 and Jacobson 1995 for the thermodynamic route, Deser–Levin 1997 for the de Sitter Unruh temperature, and Kaplinghat & Turner 2002 as the CDM account of cH0. None of the MDM papers cites an earlier statement, by anyone, that dark matter is the dual or conjugate counterpart of visible matter. Within the school, the precursors are: the first pointer from MDM to the Freidel–Leigh–Minic reformulations, 4 Jan 2016 (1601.00662), before which the 2010–2013 MDM texts never mention Freidel, metastrings or metaparticles (count 0); the metastring zero-mode sector as a model of MDM quanta, 13 Sep 2017 (1709.04388); 'metaparticles ... two entangled particles in momentum space', 30 Dec 2017 (1801.00160; the cited Freidel–Leigh–Minic papers 1707.00312 and 1706.03305 never mention dark matter); and MDM quanta as the metaparticle (dual) cousins of Standard Model fields, 29 Feb 2020 (Minic 2003.00318). All precede the program's first written statement of C1 (lab notebook v0.1, September 2026). On my papers, the priority for the identification stays with Minic 2020; the 2016–2017 MDM papers are earlier steps toward it, not statements of it.

contradicts_record.record_says: review/literature-check/findings.json, C1 finding for 2005.08927, field 'difference': "Its dark matter knows about the baryons through a0, a non-gravitational correlation against strict P4."
contradicts_record.source_says: 2005.08927, essay text: "At this point in time, Occam's razor would favor the first option" (the first option being "The scale is emergent in the" ΛCDM model); the metaparticle passage opens "Let us speculate: The BTFR and BFJR imply that the dark matter mass profile knows about the baryonic mass profile, the acceleration scale"; and the first paragraph defines CDM as "non-relativistic (Cold) and that it only interacts with the baryonic matter (and itself) gravitationally."
contradicts_record.why: The record overstates the source. The essay presents the a0 correlation as an observational fact, prefers for now its emergence within gravity-only ΛCDM, and offers the Λ-aware, metaparticle reading only as a labelled speculation. It never calls the correlation non-gravitational, so 'a non-gravitational correlation against strict P4' is the record's inference. Both passages are already in v1 (18 May 2020).

contradicts_record.record_says: review/literature-check/findings.json, the C1 findings' 'difference' field (for example the finding for 2407.06207): "(2) Coupling: the dual (dark) sector is 'correlated'/'entangled' with visible matter through non-gravitational terms and is tied to modified dark matter's acceleration-scale correlation with baryons; the school expects it to be detectable."
contradicts_record.source_says: MDM's own papers: "Despite its appearance, Eq. (18) does not modify General Relativity (GR) since the derivation of the right-hand-side is based on GR." and the information on cH0 "is conveyed to the dark-matter via the temperature of the de Sitter horizon"; "This choice is, of course, arbitrary and a case of reverse engineering." (1601.00662 §1.3); "how strongly coupled is MDM to baryonic matter and how does MDM self-interact?" (1602.00055 §1); "Whether such a dark matter profile can be realized dynamically will depend on the detailed nature of the MDM quanta and their interactions with ordinary matter." (1308.3252 §II); "with the gravitational potential providing a link between the baryonic and dark matter" (2405.08744). The tie is made on the string side: "Such a correlation between visible and dark matter involving an IR scale (in this case, the Hubble scale) has been observed in astronomical data and has been studied in the context of modified dark matter in [18]." (2010.15610 §3).
contradicts_record.why: This qualifies the record. The non-gravitational terms exist, but in the string-side papers: Minic 2020's Berry-phase-like term and Berglund–Hübsch–Minić 2021's mixing term ∝ λ⁸/L¹⁰. The MDM correlation they are tied to has no interaction term in its own papers. It is an observed regularity plus a reverse-engineered, Λ-dependent mass profile in unmodified GR, with the coupling to baryons an open question; in the 2024 fuzzy-dark-matter account the link is gravitational. The tie between the two is the school's proposal of 2020–2021 (Minic 2020; BHM 2021; Edmonds, Minic and Takeuchi 2021), not a result of MDM. The record's sentence can be read as if MDM's correlation were evidence for the non-gravitational terms; on MDM's own papers it is not.

contradicts_record.record_says: notes/literature-check.md §3, 'What differs', the coupling: "All three judges for C1 read this as predicting couplings between dark and visible matter beyond gravity: Minic 2020 expects dark quanta to be detectable through a Berry-phase-like entanglement with visible matter, and Berglund, Hübsch and Minić 2021 a dual photon correlated with ours, correlated events at accelerators and a dark–visible correlation at the Hubble scale, which they tie to modified dark matter."
contradicts_record.source_says: 2005.08927: "A correlation between the total dark matter and total baryonic matter in a region surrounding a galaxy is to be expected in the" ΛCDM scenario, and "At this point in time, Occam's razor would favor the first option"; 2009.12915 §V: "The simplest one is, of course, that it is emergent in the standard" ΛCDM model; 1709.04388 §1: "Nevertheless, it may be possible to reconcile this result with CDM models".
contradicts_record.why: This qualifies the record. The Hubble-scale dark–visible correlation that BHM tie to MDM is, by the MDM authors' own account, possibly reproduced by gravity-only ΛCDM. So the observable the school offers does not by itself separate a coupling beyond gravity from the program's gravity-only sector (#11 P4 strict, §13 row 7). The judges' reading holds for the string-side mixing and entanglement terms, not for the MDM correlation as evidence. This bears on the record's open question of whether observation can tell the two dark sectors apart. The discriminators the school proposes are a0 in colliding clusters (2005.08927), a redshift dependence of a0 (2405.08744), an acceleration floor in galaxies but not clusters (1801.00160) and a central turnover of the MDM density (1308.3252).

contradicts_record.record_says: review/literature-check/findings.json, C1 finding for 2407.06207, field 'difference': "New here: dark matter as fuzzy (non-commuting with visible fields), linked to fuzzy-dark-matter phenomenology (cf. Edmonds, Erlich, Minic, Takeuchi 2024, arXiv:2405.08744)."
contradicts_record.source_says: 2405.08744: "particles, perhaps axion-like, with de Broglie wavelength around" (10²–10³) parsecs, and "with the gravitational potential providing a link between the baryonic and dark matter, which ultimately leads to the Tully-Fisher relation"; the essay contains no 'dual', 'metaparticle', 'metastring', 'Born' or 'non-commut' (counts 0). The link is made in 2407.06207 §3.4: "Metaparticles can be understood as fuzzy dark matter, which in turn does point to a natural relation of vacuum energy (dark energy) and fuzzy dark matter" [47, 48], where [48] = 2405.08744.
contradicts_record.why: This qualifies the record. 'Fuzzy' has two senses here: Hübsch–Minić's non-commutativity of visible and dual fields, and the 2024 essay's ordinary ultralight-boson wave dark matter, with an ħ-dependent quantum pressure and a gravity-only link to the baryons. The record's 'cf.' points to a paper that does not state the dual-sector reading. The identification of metaparticles with fuzzy dark matter is Hübsch and Minić's, and the essay's own dark–baryon tie is gravitational, consistent with #11 P4.
